actual_reviewers.review_body: How can I change the title ? It has to begin with [locale]

I haven't reviewed this in a lot of detail, but I can say I'm not impressed with the API.
* I'd remove the `trunc` flag
* I'd dump the list of parse tokens and regex modification (this is getting turing complete here).
* I'd make the default patterns easily modifiable (globally and per invocation)
* I didn't get the `*` thing that is supposed to trim but is not tested, and does not trim
* I'm not so sure about the callback function -- I didn't get it and I don't thing it fits there. If anything, we can provide an iterator function for all durations, that could be passed a separate info about index of this token, so you could implement something like this, but this here is totally out of hand for a format function.
* not sure about the negative precision

I want to know what the rest of the team things, in the mean time I'm not very eager of merging this, without making sure it does what we want it to do, sanely. Everyone pressed enough is already using the plugin, so need to hurry.

actual_reviewers.review_body:
When I was reviewing two things popped to my mind:
* we need to provide an interface for users to check if the moment is mutable or not (because with 3.x and 2.x out in the wild it will be hard to tell)
* we need to do somehow test that moment is actually immutable (that is -- all functions don't change anything). Even if it is now, we'll have trouble keeping it this way just by "looking at the code".

The one thing that still bothers me with the code itself is the way we make changes to internals, just after clone in a bunch of methods (places where we call new Moment(...)). In the places where we modify _d, couldn't we just take _d, clone it, modify it and then create a moment with it -- so modify *before* clone, not after. Now this is dangerous because could mess something up, when its spread to many places (12 right now). On the other hand we can ship this way and work our way toward all-mutability-in-constructor in future (not necessarily major) versions.
